notes_for_editor: Record structures say 22.0 m for the tower, but Lighthouse Friends and Pepper give 80 ft (24 m) and NPS 82 ft; worth a human check. Sources disagree on when the lens arrived (April vs 22 June 1901), when the timber tower was removed (1901, 1903, 1904), fog-signal appropriation (Light-House Board $5,500 on 3 March 1890; Pepper $5,000 on 2 March), and the diaphone date (1925 NPS, 1926 Pepper, 13 April 1927 Lighthouse Friends; the story gives the latter two only); the story states these. Scan-page numbers are archive.org scan pages, not printed pages; the 1896-97 entry had no page index. The Marjorie Bard rescue and the McLean family detail rest on Lighthouse Friends (the Milwaukee Journal of 1 October 1939 was not read). Bulletin index entries mention keepers reaching shore over ice (c. 1919-23) and Devils Island keepers stranded by ice (1924-29); those issue pages were not read and are not in the story. Dates in the Evening Star of 22 August 1928 and the Bulletin (22 August) are not fully reconciled; the story gives the Bulletin's date. Roster: names, years and open-ended spans copied from the USLHS archive; Lighthouse Friends spells some names differently (Horron for Herron, Walter Parker, Gordon for George Gatton). Keepers listed to 1962 as principal keepers, though NPS says the Coast Guard replaced the Bureau in 1939. The 'eighth' lighthouse count in Lighthouse Friends was not repeated. Pepper dates the end of condemnation to August (after the June 1896 act, i.e. 1896); the Board's FY1896 report says the award was paid August 1895; the story states both.
